  "narrative_text": "The differentially abundant metabolite set is strongly enriched for sulfur amino acid metabolism and connected one-carbon folate cycling. Across three independent paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-network activity — the cluster centered on L-methionine, L-cysteine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH), and 2-oxobutanoate emerged as the dominant biological signal. MetaboAnalystR identified KEGG:hsa00270 (Cysteine and methionine metabolism) as the top-ranked KEGG hit (p=2×10⁻⁴, 4/33 pathway compounds) and KEGG:hsa00670 (One carbon pool by folate) co-ranked immediately below (p=2×10⁻⁴, 3/26 compounds). KEGG:hsa00480 (Glutathione metabolism) was the third KEGG hit (p=7.8×10⁻³). RaMP independently reproduced this sulfur-cluster finding: KEGG:map00260 (Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism) scored FDR=3.86×10⁻¹⁴ with the same four driver metabolites, and WP:WP2525 (Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways) ranked eighth with FDR=1.16×10⁻¹¹. Mummichog corroborated these results at the empirical-network level: 'Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism' was the top network hit (p=0.0039, 7/7 overlap) and 'Methionine and cysteine metabolism' ranked fourth (p=0.0297, 4/4 overlap). L-methionine and L-cysteine are the canonical substrates for cysteine generation and downstream glutathione synthesis, while 2-oxobutanoate (a threonine/valine catabolite) feeds the one-carbon pool. react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolite set is strongly enriched for sulfur amino acid metabolism and connected one-carbon folate cycling. Across three independent paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-network activity — the cluster centered on L-methionine, L-cysteine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH), and 2-oxobutanoate emerged as the dominant biological signal. MetaboAnalystR identified KEGG:hsa00270 (Cysteine and methionine metabolism) as the top-ranked KEGG hit (p=2×10⁻⁴, 4/33 pathway compounds) and KEGG:hsa00670 (One carbon pool by folate) co-ranked immediately below (p=2×10⁻⁴, 3/26 compounds). KEGG:hsa00480 (Glutathione metabolism) was the third KEGG hit (p=7.8×10⁻³). RaMP independently reproduced this sulfur-cluster finding: KEGG:map00260 (Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism) scored FDR=3.86×10⁻¹⁴ with the same four driver metabolites, and WP:WP2525 (Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways) ranked eighth with FDR=1.16×10⁻¹¹. Mummichog corroborated these results at the empirical-network level: 'Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism' was the top network hit (p=0.0039, 7/7 overlap) and 'Methionine and cysteine metabolism' ranked fourth (p=0.0297, 4/4 overlap). The biological story is one of disrupted methyl-group cycling and trans-sulfuration: SAH is the product of every S-adenosylmethionine (SAM)-dependent methyltransferase reaction, and its accumulation signals either increased global DNA/histone methylation activity or impaired adenosine-to-homocysteine-to-cysteine flux. L-methionine and L-cysteine are the canonical substrates for cysteine generation and downstream glutathione synthesis, while 2-oxobutanoate (a threonine/valine catabolite) feeds the one-carbon pool. The simultaneous elevation of (R)-lipoic acid (a cofactor for pyruvate dehydrogenase and other multienzyme complexes requiring acyl-group transfer) and L-ornithine (urea cycle) suggests broader perturbation of nitrogen and energy metabolism co-occurring with the sulfur-amino-acid disruption. Phenylephrine, nitrate, and 5,6-dihydroxyindole did not contribute significantly to the top-ranked pathways but may represent secondary signaling or oxidative-stress responses.

RaMP multi-database ORA identified KEGG:map00260 (Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism) as the top hit with FDR=3.86×10⁻¹⁴ and 6 metabolites overlapping (L-ornithine, 2-oxobutanoate, (R)-lipoic acid, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, L-cysteine, L-methionine). WikiPathways WP:WP2525 (Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways) ranked eighth in the same analysis with FDR=1.16×10⁻¹¹ and 5 overlapping metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently reproduced a sulfur-amino-acid signal: KEGG:hsa00670 (One carbon pool by folate) was the top-ranked KEGG hit with p-value 0.0002 and 3 overlapping metabolites (L-methionine, SAH, L-cysteine), followed by KEGG:hsa00480 (Glutathione metabolism) at p=0.0078 and KEGG:hsa00260 (Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism) at p=0.0108. Mummichog m/z-network activity corroborated these results: Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism (MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism) ranked first with p=0.0036 and 7 overlapping metabolites, and Urea cycle/amino group metabolism (MUMM:urea_cycle_amino_group_metabolism) co-ranked first. Methionine and cysteine metabolism (MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism) ranked fourth with p=0.029 and full 4/4 overlap of the input sulfur metabolites (SAH, L-methionine, L-cysteine, 2-oxobutanoate). L-methionine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, L-cysteine and 2-oxobutanoate are confirmed members of Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism via KEGG:map00260 (6/57 overlap) and of Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways via WP:WP2525 (5/60 overlap). The cross-paradigm winner is the glycine/serine/threonine cluster at the intersection of one-carbon folate cycling and sulfur amino acid trans-sulfuration, with L-methionine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine and L-cysteine as the primary driver metabolites linking these two subsystems.

react_result.final_narrative_text: RaMP multi-database ORA, Mummichog m/z-network activity, and Reactome ORA all converged on amino-acid and methyl-group metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP identified KEGG:map00260 (Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism) as the top hit with FDR=3.86×10⁻¹⁴, with 6 input metabolites overlapping: L-ornithine (KEGG:C00077), 2-oxobutanoate (KEGG:C00109), (R)-lipoic acid (KEGG:C16241), S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (KEGG:C00021), L-cysteine (KEGG:C00097), and L-methionine (KEGG:C00073). WikiPathways WP:WP2525 (Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways) ranked eighth in RaMP with FDR=1.16×10⁻¹¹ and 5 overlapping metabolites: L-ornithine, 2-oxobutanoate, SAH, L-cysteine, and L-methionine. Mummichog m/z-network activity independently reproduced the signal: MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism ranked first with p=0.0040 and full 7/7 overlap, MUMM:urea_cycle_amino_group_metabolism co-ranked first with identical p-value and full 7/7 overlap, and MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism ranked fourth with p=0.026 and full 4/4 overlap. Reactome REACT:R-HSA-71291 (Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives) ranked ninth in RaMP with FDR=7.94×10⁻¹¹. Cross-paradigm consensus identifies glycine/serine/threonine/alanine metabolism, urea cycle/amino-group metabolism, and methionine/cysteine metabolism as the affected modules, with S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine and L-methionine as the primary driver metabolites linking trans-sulfuration and one-carbon cycling.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: RaMP multi-database ORA, Mummichog m/z-network activity, and Reactome ORA all converged on amino-acid and methyl-group metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP identified KEGG:map00260 (Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism) as the top hit with FDR=3.86×10⁻¹⁴, with 6 input metabolites overlapping: L-ornithine (KEGG:C00077), 2-oxobutanoate (KEGG:C00109), (R)-lipoic acid (KEGG:C16241), S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (KEGG:C00021), L-cysteine (KEGG:C00097), and L-methionine (KEGG:C00073). WikiPathways WP:WP2525 (Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways) ranked eighth in RaMP with FDR=1.16×10⁻¹¹ and 5 overlapping metabolites: L-ornithine, 2-oxobutanoate, SAH, L-cysteine, and L-methionine. Mummichog m/z-network activity independently reproduced the signal: MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism ranked first with p=0.0040 and full 7/7 overlap, MUMM:urea_cycle_amino_group_metabolism co-ranked first with identical p-value and full 7/7 overlap, and MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism ranked fourth with p=0.026 and full 4/4 overlap. Reactome REACT:R-HSA-71291 (Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives) ranked ninth in RaMP with FDR=7.94×10⁻¹¹. Cross-paradigm consensus identifies glycine/serine/threonine/alanine metabolism, urea cycle/amino-group metabolism, and methionine/cysteine metabolism as the affected modules, with S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine and L-methionine as the primary driver metabolites linking trans-sulfuration and one-carbon cycling.
